Why Do Bank Statement Charges Look Like Gibberish?

REASON 01

22 characters, no mercy

Card networks give merchants a name field roughly 22 characters long. Real names get amputated into initials and codes that only make sense once you know the trick.

VALVOLINE INSTANT OIL CHANGE → VIOC LB0134

REASON 02

The middleman signs the receipt

Millions of small businesses run cards through Square, Toast, or Paddle. Your statement names the processor first — the actual seller is squeezed in after an asterisk.

SQ *BLU BTL COF · TST* HG HOLDINGS

Decode the SQ * prefix →

REASON 03

Companies bill under names you've never heard

OnlyFans bills as Fenix Internet. Your building's laundry room bills as CSC ServiceWorks. Comcast autopay shows up as ACHMA VISB. None of this is on purpose to help you.

  3. Contact the merchant behind the descriptor — refunds there take days, disputes take weeks.
  4. Still nothing? Lock the card and call your bank — 60-day dispute windows apply.

The Unknown Charge Lookup Tool

How to Identify an Unknown Charge on Your Credit Card

When you look at your monthly statement and think, "what is this charge on my credit card," you aren't alone. Unrecognized or unknown charges are incredibly common. Sometimes they are genuine cases of unauthorized credit card charges, but often, they are simply legitimate purchases obscured by a confusing billing descriptor. Our credit card merchant lookup tool is designed to decode these cryptic bank charges, helping you identify exactly who charged your account.

What Are Bank Charges and Payment Descriptors?

A payment descriptor (or billing descriptor) is the text that appears on your bank or credit card statement to identify a transaction. Card networks restrict this field to around 22 characters. Consequently, businesses often use acronyms, store numbers, or the name of their payment processor instead of their recognizable storefront name. For instance, an Amazon unknown charge might appear as AMZN MKTP, or a small business might use SQ* for a Square payment.

By performing a charge lookup, you can translate these payment descriptors into the actual merchant's name. We maintain an extensive list of bank charges, covering everything from streaming subscriptions to credit card charges for business software. Unlike crowdsourced forums, UnknownCharges relies on original data journalism and offline verification by parsing primary records, including Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) complaints, ensuring you get accurate answers rather than guesses.

Common Sources of Unknown Transactions

Before panicking over a suspicious charge, consider the most frequent culprits behind an unknown payment:

  • Payment Processors: Middlemen like Square, PayPal, or Stripe often prepend their initials (e.g., SQ* or PP*).
  • Parent Companies: You might buy from a local boutique, but the transaction description reflects the parent LLC.
  • Subscriptions and Free Trials: A small unknown charge is often a forgotten subscription auto-renewing.
  • Digital Wallets: An unknown charge from Facebook or Apple might be a digital purchase made by a family member sharing your account.

Use our transaction lookup to cross-reference these scenarios and definitively identify the merchant. If your search doesn't match a known descriptor, browse the full ledger by category or check the prefix and bank hubs.

Disputing Unauthorized Credit Card and Debit Card Charges

If you use our merchant search and confirm the transaction isn't yours, you must act quickly. Disputing credit card charges protects you from financial loss due to fraud. But how long do you have to dispute credit card charges? Under the Fair Credit Billing Act (FCBA), you have 60 days from the date the statement containing the error was sent to you. Disputing bank charges on a debit card falls under Regulation E, which generally requires reporting within two business days to limit your liability to $50, or within 60 days to avoid unlimited liability for subsequent unauthorized transfers. Use our dispute window calculator to determine your exact deadline.

Steps to Resolve an Unknown Transaction

  1. Search the exact text: Paste the exact statement text into our charge lookup tool at the top of the page.
  2. Review your receipts: Cross-reference the amount and date with your email receipts to jog your memory.
  3. Check with family: Ask authorized users if they recognize the purchase, especially on shared accounts.
  4. Contact the merchant: If the merchant search reveals a legitimate business you recognize but didn't authorize a purchase from, contacting them directly is often faster than a bank dispute.
  5. File a dispute: If it is truly an unauthorized credit card charge, lock your card and call your bank's fraud department immediately. Read the unknown-charge playbook for a full walkthrough.

Quick answers

Frequently Asked Questions About Credit Card Charges & Subscriptions

What is this charge on my credit card?

An unrecognized charge on your credit card or bank statement usually stems from a parent company billing under a different corporate name, a payment processor prefix (like SQ*, TST*, or AMZN MKTP), a forgotten recurring subscription, or a temporary authorization hold. Paste the exact statement line into our lookup tool above to identify the underlying merchant.

Why do I have an Adobe charge on my credit card?

An unexpected Adobe charge (such as ADOBE *PHOTOG, ADOBE *CREATIVE, or ADOBE 800-833-6687) typically occurs when a free trial converts into an annual subscription billed monthly, a plan auto-renews, or a secondary user on your account licensed stock assets. You can review active subscriptions at account.adobe.com/plans or see our Adobe charge guide.

How to dispute a credit card charge?

To dispute a credit card charge under the Fair Credit Billing Act (FCBA), first gather transaction receipts and check if the line is pending or settled. If unauthorized or erroneous, submit a written or digital dispute to your card issuer within 60 calendar days of the statement mailing date. Use our dispute letter generator and dispute window calculator for formal notice.

What is a charge off on a credit card?

A credit card charge off occurs when a creditor writes off a delinquent balance as an uncollectible accounting loss, typically after 180 consecutive days without payment. A charge off does not erase the legal obligation to pay: the card issuer may assign or sell the account to a third-party debt collection agency. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), a charged-off account remains on credit bureau files for up to 7 years from the date of the original delinquency.

What is a charge card vs credit card?

The primary difference between a charge card and a credit card is the repayment structure: a charge card requires the entire balance to be paid in full each month with no preset spending limit and no revolving balance, while a credit card provides a set credit limit and allows you to carry an unpaid balance subject to interest.

Can you dispute a debit card charge?

Yes, you can dispute a debit card charge under federal law through the Electronic Fund Transfer Act (Regulation E, 12 CFR § 1005.11). For unauthorized transactions, notifying your financial institution within 2 business days limits your maximum liability to $50; reporting between 3 and 60 calendar days from statement delivery caps liability at $500. For merchant billing errors, banks must investigate and typically issue provisional credit within 10 business days.

How long do charge-offs stay on your credit report?

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), a charge-off stays on your credit report for up to 7 years from the date of initial delinquency (the first missed payment that led to the default). Paying or settling the charged-off balance updates the entry status to Paid or Settled Charge-Off, but does not reset or extend the 7-year removal date.

How to cancel Adobe subscription?

To cancel an Adobe subscription: (1) Sign in to account.adobe.com/plans. (2) Select Manage Plan on your active subscription. (3) Click Cancel your plan and choose a reason. (4) Review any early cancellation fee disclosures for annual plans paid monthly, then confirm cancellation. You can also generate formal notice with our cancellation generator.

How to cancel subscription on iPhone?

To cancel an Apple-billed subscription on iPhone: (1) Open the Settings app. (2) Tap your name (Apple ID) at the top. (3) Tap Subscriptions. (4) Tap the active subscription you wish to terminate. (5) Tap Cancel Subscription (or Cancel Free Trial) and confirm. Service continues until the end of the current billing period. See our Apple billing reference.

How to cancel ChatGPT subscription?

To cancel a ChatGPT Plus or Team subscription: (1) Log in to chatgpt.com on a web browser. (2) Click your profile icon in the bottom-left sidebar. (3) Select Settings, then navigate to My Plan (or Account). (4) Click Manage my subscription to open the Stripe billing portal. (5) Select Cancel Plan and confirm. See our ChatGPT charge guide.

How to cancel Canva subscription?

To cancel a Canva Pro or Canva Teams subscription: (1) Log in to canva.com on desktop or mobile browser. (2) Click the Gear icon (Account settings) in the top-right corner. (3) Select Billing & plans from the sidebar. (4) Next to your active plan, click More actions (...) and select Cancel subscription. (5) Confirm the cancellation steps. See our Canva charge reference.

How to cancel Fubo subscription?

To cancel a Fubo (FuboTV) subscription: (1) Sign in at fubo.tv on a web browser. (2) Click your profile icon and select My Account. (3) Select Subscription & Billing. (4) Scroll to the bottom and click Cancel Subscription. (5) Click Complete Cancellation and select a reason. See our Fubo charge reference.

How to cancel Hulu subscription?

To cancel a Hulu subscription: (1) Go to hulu.com/account and log in. (2) Scroll down to the Your Subscription section. (3) Click Cancel next to Cancel Your Subscription. (4) Select Continue to Cancel to bypass temporary pause promotions. (5) Select a cancellation reason and confirm. See our Hulu charge reference.

How to Identify an Unknown Charge on Your Credit Card
When you look at your monthly statement and think, "what is this charge on my credit card," you aren't alone. Unrecognized or unknown charges are incredibly common. Sometimes they are genuine cases of unauthorized credit card charges, but often, they are simply legitimate purchases obscured by a confusing billing descriptor. Our credit card merchant lookup tool is designed to decode these cryptic bank charges, helping you identify exactly who charged your account.
What Are Bank Charges and Payment Descriptors?
A payment descriptor (or billing descriptor) is the text that appears on your bank or credit card statement to identify a transaction. Card networks restrict this field to around 22 characters. Consequently, businesses often use acronyms, store numbers, or the name of their payment processor instead of their recognizable storefront name. For instance, an Amazon unknown charge might appear as AMZN MKTP, or a small business might use SQ* for a Square payment.
By performing a charge lookup, you can translate these payment descriptors into the actual merchant's name. We maintain an extensive list of bank charges, covering everything from streaming subscriptions to credit card charges for business software. Unlike crowdsourced forums, UnknownCharges relies on original data journalism and offline verification by parsing primary records, including Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) complaints, ensuring you get accurate answers rather than guesses.
Common Sources of Unknown Transactions
Before panicking over a suspicious charge, consider the most frequent culprits behind an unknown payment:
- Payment Processors: Middlemen like Square, PayPal, or Stripe often prepend their initials (e.g., SQ* or PP*).
- Parent Companies: You might buy from a local boutique, but the transaction description reflects the parent LLC.
- Subscriptions and Free Trials: A small unknown charge is often a forgotten subscription auto-renewing.
- Digital Wallets: An unknown charge from Facebook or Apple might be a digital purchase made by a family member sharing your account.
Use our transaction lookup to cross-reference these scenarios and definitively identify the merchant. If your search doesn't match a known descriptor, browse the full ledger by category or check the prefix and bank hubs.
Disputing Unauthorized Credit Card and Debit Card Charges
If you use our merchant search and confirm the transaction isn't yours, you must act quickly. Disputing credit card charges protects you from financial loss due to fraud. But how long do you have to dispute credit card charges? Under the Fair Credit Billing Act (FCBA), you have 60 days from the date the statement containing the error was sent to you. Disputing bank charges on a debit card falls under Regulation E, which generally requires reporting within two business days to limit your liability to $50, or within 60 days to avoid unlimited liability for subsequent unauthorized transfers. Use our dispute window calculator to determine your exact deadline.

Quick answers
Frequently Asked Questions About Credit Card Charges & Subscriptions
What is this charge on my credit card?
An unrecognized charge on your credit card or bank statement usually stems from a parent company billing under a different corporate name, a payment processor prefix (like SQ*, TST*, or AMZN MKTP), a forgotten recurring subscription, or a temporary authorization hold. Paste the exact statement line into our lookup tool above to identify the underlying merchant.
Why do I have an Adobe charge on my credit card?
An unexpected Adobe charge (such as ADOBE *PHOTOG, ADOBE *CREATIVE, or ADOBE 800-833-6687) typically occurs when a free trial converts into an annual subscription billed monthly, a plan auto-renews, or a secondary user on your account licensed stock assets. You can review active subscriptions at account.adobe.com/plans or see our Adobe charge guide.
How to dispute a credit card charge?
To dispute a credit card charge under the Fair Credit Billing Act (FCBA), first gather transaction receipts and check if the line is pending or settled. If unauthorized or erroneous, submit a written or digital dispute to your card issuer within 60 calendar days of the statement mailing date. Use our dispute letter generator and dispute window calculator for formal notice.
What is a charge off on a credit card?
A credit card charge off occurs when a creditor writes off a delinquent balance as an uncollectible accounting loss, typically after 180 consecutive days without payment. A charge off does not erase the legal obligation to pay: the card issuer may assign or sell the account to a third-party debt collection agency. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), a charged-off account remains on credit bureau files for up to 7 years from the date of the original delinquency.
What is a charge card vs credit card?
The primary difference between a charge card and a credit card is the repayment structure: a charge card requires the entire balance to be paid in full each month with no preset spending limit and no revolving balance, while a credit card provides a set credit limit and allows you to carry an unpaid balance subject to interest.
Can you dispute a debit card charge?
Yes, you can dispute a debit card charge under federal law through the Electronic Fund Transfer Act (Regulation E, 12 CFR § 1005.11). For unauthorized transactions, notifying your financial institution within 2 business days limits your maximum liability to $50; reporting between 3 and 60 calendar days from statement delivery caps liability at $500. For merchant billing errors, banks must investigate and typically issue provisional credit within 10 business days.
How long do charge-offs stay on your credit report?
Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), a charge-off stays on your credit report for up to 7 years from the date of initial delinquency (the first missed payment that led to the default). Paying or settling the charged-off balance updates the entry status to Paid or Settled Charge-Off, but does not reset or extend the 7-year removal date.
How to cancel Adobe subscription?
To cancel an Adobe subscription: (1) Sign in to account.adobe.com/plans. (2) Select Manage Plan on your active subscription. (3) Click Cancel your plan and choose a reason. (4) Review any early cancellation fee disclosures for annual plans paid monthly, then confirm cancellation. You can also generate formal notice with our cancellation generator.
How to cancel subscription on iPhone?
To cancel an Apple-billed subscription on iPhone: (1) Open the Settings app. (2) Tap your name (Apple ID) at the top. (3) Tap Subscriptions. (4) Tap the active subscription you wish to terminate. (5) Tap Cancel Subscription (or Cancel Free Trial) and confirm. Service continues until the end of the current billing period. See our Apple billing reference.
How to cancel ChatGPT subscription?
To cancel a ChatGPT Plus or Team subscription: (1) Log in to chatgpt.com on a web browser. (2) Click your profile icon in the bottom-left sidebar. (3) Select Settings, then navigate to My Plan (or Account). (4) Click Manage my subscription to open the Stripe billing portal. (5) Select Cancel Plan and confirm. See our ChatGPT charge guide.
How to cancel Canva subscription?
To cancel a Canva Pro or Canva Teams subscription: (1) Log in to canva.com on desktop or mobile browser. (2) Click the Gear icon (Account settings) in the top-right corner. (3) Select Billing & plans from the sidebar. (4) Next to your active plan, click More actions (...) and select Cancel subscription. (5) Confirm the cancellation steps. See our Canva charge reference.
How to cancel Fubo subscription?
To cancel a Fubo (FuboTV) subscription: (1) Sign in at fubo.tv on a web browser. (2) Click your profile icon and select My Account. (3) Select Subscription & Billing. (4) Scroll to the bottom and click Cancel Subscription. (5) Click Complete Cancellation and select a reason. See our Fubo charge reference.
How to cancel Hulu subscription?
To cancel a Hulu subscription: (1) Go to hulu.com/account and log in. (2) Scroll down to the Your Subscription section. (3) Click Cancel next to Cancel Your Subscription. (4) Select Continue to Cancel to bypass temporary pause promotions. (5) Select a cancellation reason and confirm. See our Hulu charge reference.
